sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Look at the flowchart: wash the vegetable or fruit, dry thoroughly, cut or slice on a clean board, mix with salt and spices, place in a dry sterilised container, cover with salt and/or oil, close with a tight-fitting lid and store. Identify the method and write the two main purposes of the oil used in the final step.
questions.answer: The method is pickling. Oil keeps out air and so prevents micro-organisms from entering, and it prevents the food from coming in contact with air and spoiling.

questions.q: True or False. (a) A peeled apple spoils faster than an apple with intact skin. (b) Blanching kills all enzymes permanently.
questions.answer: (a) True: the skin is a protective cover. (b) False: it stops enzyme action for a time by mild heat.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Jam is ready when a drop placed in cold water ________. (b) Bottles for squash are sterilised by boiling for ________ minutes.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Murabba (b) Jelly. B: (i) Fruit boiled in sugar syrup (ii) Strained clear juice with pectin, acid and sugar (iii) Dried vegetables.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Your mother has bought a large quantity of fresh tender peas. Suggest the correct method to freeze them for future use.
questions.answer: Shell the fresh peas and blanch them in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Cool at once, pack in polythene bags removing air, seal and keep in the freezer.

questions.q: Besides mangoes, list four ingredients used for making mango squash.
questions.answer: Sugar, water, citric acid and a preservative such as KMS or sodium benzoate (also colour and essence).

or.q: How will you check that the jam you are making is ready?
or.answer: Put a drop in a plate of cold water; if it stays in one place it is ready. Also it falls from the spoon as a flake or sheet.

questions.q: How will you prepare amla murabba at home?
questions.answer: Prick the amla and steam it for 5 minutes. Add the sugar in three portions over three days and heat the syrup till it dissolves; it is ready after 15 days.

or.q: Write the steps of making mixed vegetable pickle.
or.answer: Wash and dry the vegetables thoroughly, cut them and mix with salt and spices. Put them in a dry sterilised jar, cover with oil and close with a tight lid.

questions.q: What is food preservation? Give two reasons for preserving food.
questions.answer: It is treating food to keep it in good condition for a long time. It increases shelf life and helps use excess produce and make new products.

questions.q: How do salt and oil help in preserving pickles?
questions.answer: Salt and spices draw out water so micro-organisms cannot grow. Oil forms a layer that keeps out air and micro-organisms.

questions.q: What is blanching? Why is it done?
questions.answer: Blanching is dipping vegetables in hot water or steam for a few minutes. It stops the action of enzymes before canning or freezing.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the three principles of food preservation with examples.
questions.answer: (i) Killing micro-organisms by heat, as in boiling milk or canning. (ii) Preventing or delaying their action by covering, cooling, freezing or adding preservatives such as KMS. (iii) Stopping enzyme action by blanching or mild heat treatment before freezing.

questions.q: Suggest the best method to preserve orange juice, raw mango, potato and carrots, with a reason.
questions.answer: (i) Orange juice as squash, with sugar and a preservative. (ii) Raw mango as pickle, with salt, spices and oil. (iii) Potato as dried wafers or chips, because moisture is removed; carrots as pickle or murabba.

questions.q: Give four reasons why we should preserve food.
questions.answer: (i) To increase shelf life. (ii) To prepare new products such as jams, papads and pickles. (iii) To reduce the bulk of fruits and vegetables for storage and transport. (iv) To prevent spoilage and wastage of excess produce.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the household methods of food preservation. Explain any three with a recipe.
questions.answer: (i) The methods are drying, pickling, jams, jellies and murabbas, bottling of squashes and freezing. (ii) Drying: sun-dry blanched vegetables or potato chips (dip in salt and KMS water) covered with muslin. (iii) Pickling: wash and dry, cut, mix salt and spices, fill a dry sterilised jar, cover with oil. (iv) Jam: boil fruit pulp with sugar and citric acid till a drop sets in cold water. (v) Squash: mix juice with sugar syrup, add citric acid and KMS and bottle in sterilised bottles. (vi) Freezing: blanch peas, cool, pack without air and freeze.
